reviewed_by: Claude review of ranking connected servers alongside tools, and reusing a Jev ranking when the same request recurs
reason: tool_suggestions.py stops asking Jev the two gate questions and instead ranks the selected MCP servers in the same call as the tools. build_questions now emits sources_<i> choice questions built by source_criteria() -- a server's label plus the instructions it returned at the MCP handshake, or its tool names when it returned none -- and interpret_answers returns a JevRanking carrying per-tool probabilities, per-source probabilities and the none_of_these probability of each tool's question. rank() multiplies a tool's probability by a bounded prior from its source (floor 0.5, so a source can halve a tool's score but never silence it, and a tool whose source was not ranked stays at full weight), keeps at most MAX_PICKS=3 tools, and preloads at most two of them -- only those that also beat their question's none option, which is what now stands in for the removed gate. chat.py passes mcp_sources(mcp_profiles) and copies the ranked source labels into CatalogReceipt.source_hints; catalog_instructions names them in the per-turn text. test_tool_suggestions covers the handshake-instruction and tool-name descriptions, a source rank deciding which of two equally rated tools is preloaded, the three-pick cap, the none option holding a schema back without hiding the hint, and the prepare path recording source_hints; test_tool_catalog re-runs because it shares that fixture and owns catalog_instructions. A second commit adds SuggestionCache: ChatService holds one and suggest_tools consults it before calling out, keyed by request_key() -- a sha256 over the model name, the state (operator request, earlier messages, selected skill instructions) and the questions (every tool name and summary, every source criterion). The catalog alone cannot be the key because a ranking answers one request, so the next message misses, as does a new MCP server or a re-probed description. Unavailable receipts are never stored, a hit is marked cached and reports input_tokens None, and the OrderedDict keeps the newest 64 entries in-process. Tests cover the hit, the four ways to miss, that a failed call is not cached, LRU eviction, and that ChatService.prepare populates the cache. Rebased onto #417 and #416; the selected suites were re-run on that base (75 passed).
exclusions: No frontend unit tests and no UI change: ToolSuggestionChip reads status/preloaded/suggested, which keep their meaning, and the new sources key is ignored by the client type until a chip mockup is approved. No native tests: no Tauri or Rust change. No screenshot baselines: no rendered surface changes. Playwright is area:tool-suggestions only (its four catalogued entries, 7 tests). The impact rules would also pull area:assistant, area:chat-edit-in-place and area:provider-thinking for chat.py, but the change there is three lines inside the Jev-only block that neither the chat stream, message editing nor thinking rendering touches; area:core-api is excluded because no request or response schema changes -- the turn snapshot and the chip payload only gain optional keys. tests/v3/test_chat.py, test_chat_api.py and test_mcp_probe.py were run locally (76 passed) and are excluded as unaffected.
